subject: Post-demo performance readiness checklist & harness handoff
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo performance readiness checklist & harness handoff

Hi Daniel / Priya — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick written recap and concrete next steps so we have alignment before the hands-on benchmark run.

Summary of what we covered verbally:
- BlueArc target SLOs: P50 and P95 latency targets, expected concurrency and sustained throughput, and streaming behavior for partial-result use cases.
- Redwood will provide an evaluation harness (reproducible runner, prompt set, measurement defs) and suggested config (batching/kv-cache/quantization).
- Two-phase validation: 1) lab qualification (deterministic harness runs), 2) production-ish stress with your traffic profile.

What we need from BlueArc to proceed:
1) Confirm latency SLOs (P50 / P95) you want to qualify against.
2) Provide a representative traffic CSV (timestamps + request sizes) or a short sampling of event-driven streaming sessions.
3) Clarify whether end-to-end (browser->app->model) or server-side (model request) latency is the primary metric.

What we will deliver before the tech sync:
- Redwood: redwood-benchmark-harness-v1.yaml (attached) + sample-prompts-v1.json with the golden prompt set.
- Measurement definitions document (in the shared Drive link below).
- A runnable container image and a short reproduction script.

Proposed timeline / next steps:
- Please confirm SLO numbers and share traffic sample by EOW (Feb 18).
- Tech benchmark call (60 min) to run through harness and initial run: suggested slot Feb 21–23.

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-harness-v1.yaml (harness config), sample-prompts-v1.json (example prompts).

If you prefer, we can split the first session into: 20m architecture + 40m hands-on. Let me know which you prefer.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 01:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo performance readiness checklist & harness handoff

Neha — thanks for the clear notes. Quick answers from our side:
- Targets: P50 <= 120ms, P95 <= 350ms (server-side model request to model-response complete).
- Concurrency: baseline 40 concurrent active requests, burst to 150 for short spikes.
- Sustained throughput target: ~400 req/s during peak testing window.
- Streaming: yes, we need chunked partial responses for user-facing chat (latency requirement applies to first-byte and final-byte separately).

We will attach a sample traffic file (bluearc_traffic_profile.csv) with timestamps and sizes by EOD tomorrow. Also adding our infra contact (infra@bluearc.com) who will help with network/VPC questions.

One operational note: procurement asks that any test container with customer data runs only within our approved VPC or on-prem test hosts — we'll flag the hosts in advance.

Happy to do the Feb 21 slot for the hands-on; 60m sounds good.

— Daniel
Director, Platform Engineering
BlueArc Systems
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@bluearc.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@bluearc.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 04:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo performance readiness checklist & harness handoff

Daniel — appreciate the targets. A few technical clarifications and a proposed measurement definition so everyone's on the same page before the run:

Measurement definitions (proposed):
- "Model request latency": time from Redwood API receive timestamp to final model-token emitted (server-side). This excludes network hop to client.
- "First-byte latency": time from model request receive to the first token emitted when streaming is enabled.
- P95/P50 calculation method: wall-clock latency per request after warmup, using the exact sample set of requests from the provided CSV. We will include median / 99th as optional.

Reproducibility steps we'll include in the harness: seed fixed RNG, deterministic sampling of prompt permutations, KV-cache warmup profile (100 warmup requests per worker), and a defined cold-start sweep (0->workers). We'll version the harness YAML and include exact container tags.

Quick config suggestions for the initial lab pass (to reduce variance):
- Disable quantization and enable float32 runtime for baseline accuracy & latency parity.
- Use fixed batch size = 1 for latency measurement runs; we will run separate throughput tests with batching tuned.
- Pin CPU/GPU clocks where possible on your hosts — we will provide commands for the hosts you will run.

I uploaded the initial harness folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_harness (contains the runner script and measurement-defs.md).

Can you confirm that the "server-side model request" definition above matches what you expect for the SLOs? If you prefer end-to-end, we will add an additional client-side measurement.

-Karthik
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
